caption: An observer facing the target cell: any real change of that block (placed, removed, a property changed, even by shape updates alone, as crops grow) fires it 2 gt later for 2 gt. A pure block update changes nothing there, so it is not seen; a change while its tick is pending or while it is on is missed (re-arm 4 gt). Silent.

The observer-free BUD, armed by quasi-connectivity: a sticky piston facing up under a slime block and a redstone block. The redstone block powers the piston only through the cell above it, and nothing updates the piston when that power is there, so it sits armed until a block update reaches its cell (a block placed, removed or changed beside it, or a pure update). Then it extends: the slime block lifts the redstone block beside the output for 1 gt, where it no longer powers the piston; the landing slime block updates the piston through its head, it retracts and pulls both back, the redstone block landing last, so the piston is armed again without an update. A shape-only change sends no block update: not detected. Two updates 2 gt apart jam it.

A presence detector: a fence beside the target connects to a solid block there (its shape follows its neighbors) and an observer watches the fence. Placing or removing a block at the target changes the connection and fires the observer; turning the block in place, a shape-only change or a pure update leaves the connection as it was. The fence's other two free sides sense too.
